name: Episodic Memory Theory
citation: Tulving, E. (1972). Episodic and semantic memory. In E. Tulving & W. Donaldson (Eds.), Organization of memory (pp. 381-403). Academic Press.
rejection_rationale: T1-adjacency problem with the MS (Memory Systems) framework. At 3.4% template coverage, it lacks the template mass for formal reduction. More critically, episodic memory is fundamentally a T1 mechanism (hippocampal encoding, consolidation, retrieval) rather than a domain-level environmental theory. Its environmental applications (place memory, biographical attachment) are better captured within Place Attachment. Path forward: develop as a component mechanism within existing T1.5 theories rather than as independent T1.5.
key_references: Tulving, E. (1972). Organization of memory. Academic Press.

function_form.function_form: M(e, t) = S(e)·exp(-t/τ) + R(e,ctx); R = f(hippocampal_replay, cue_match)

variables.M(e,t): Memory strength of episode e at time t
variables.\u03c4: Decay time constant (~days for hippocampal, ~years for neocortical)

predictions: Emotionally arousing environments improve later recognition ~40%
Context-dependent retrieval: return to encoding location boosts recall ~25%

provenance.seminal_paper: Tulving, E. (1972). Episodic and semantic memory. In E. Tulving & W. Donaldson (Eds.), Organization of memory (pp. 381-403). New York: Academic Press.
provenance.major_opus: Tulving, E. (1983). Elements of episodic memory. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
provenance.predecessor: Early memory research in experimental psychology; information processing models; distinction implicit in Hebb's cell assemblies
provenance.historical_context: Tulving's 1972 chapter distinguished episodic memory (memory for events with spatial-temporal context) from semantic memory (general knowledge and facts). This distinction was revolutionary in cognitive psychology, challenging monolithic memory models. The distinction enabled 500+ citations by 1983, and his 1983 opus Elements of Episodic Memory provided comprehensive theoretical development. Key innovation: autonoetic consciousness enabling 'mental time travel' — ability to deliberately project oneself to specific times and places.
key_milestones: 1972: Seminal publication of episodic/semantic distinction in Organization of Memory
1983: Comprehensive theoretical work, Elements of Episodic Memory
1985-2000: Neurobiological validation via fMRI studies of memory systems
1990s-Present: Discovery of neural correlates (hippocampal replay, reinstatement)
2000s-Present: Integration with neuroscience and consciousness research
influenced_by: Experimental psychology tradition questioning S-R behaviorism
provenance.current_status: foundational and actively researched; core concept in cognitive neuroscience
provenance.verification_notes: Seminal paper verified via Organization of Memory (1972) and PubMed/Google Scholar (50,000+ citations). Tulving (1983) opus verified. Citation trajectory confirmed (500+ by 1983). Neuroscientific validation timeline based on fMRI emergence in 1990s and place cell research history.
